headline: Highest risk is TREK’s browser/MCP-enabled, collaborative defaults creating medium-severity leakage and cascading-error pathways when paired with RisingWave’s file/network-safe posture.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RisingWave shows no shared channel or input surface, while TREK has browser and MCP access plus real-time collaboration. That makes prompt injection plausible only if TREK content is manually or programmatically bridged into RisingWave, which is not documented here. The pathway is therefore limited and not default.
conditions: IF TREK outputs are copied into RisingWave prompts or files
IF a shared MCP or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted TREK content into RisingWave
Add a manual review step before any TREK-generated text is reused
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any bridged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and documents, and it writes to local files and logs. RisingWave is documented as network-egress none, so it is not an obvious exfiltrator, but the pair still creates a shared-data risk if TREK files or outputs are moved into RisingWave workflows. The interaction is plausible in default collaborative use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF TREK data files or logs are imported into RisingWave processing
IF either agent is granted access to the same workspace or mounted volume
mitigations: Store TREK secrets in a separate vault
Do not mount TREK uploads or logs into RisingWave jobs
Review any exported TREK artifacts before reuse
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RisingWave has no documented write or network surfaces here, while TREK supports real-time collaboration and multiple instances. Because the profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains, so the lower severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or database
IF TREK instances are run concurrently against the same mutable state
mitigations: Assign separate storage paths per agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same TREK database
Use a single orchestrator for state changes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is explicitly a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream content as actionable. RisingWave can produce data-engineering outputs, but no verification boundary between the agents is documented. If RisingWave output is fed into TREK as authoritative travel facts, downstream actions could be wrong or misleading.
conditions: IF RisingWave output is ingested by TREK without validation
IF TREK uses RisingWave-produced text as authoritative travel guidance
mitigations: Require human review before acting on cross-agent outputs
Add schema validation for any RisingWave-to-TREK handoff
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted in TREK prompts
Log and diff any reused facts before execution
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: TREK clearly handles secrets, reservations, documents, and logs, while RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no residency or retention controls shown. The pair therefore has a compliance mismatch risk if TREK data is processed or retained under RisingWave workflows. RisingWave is the only agent with no stated compliance controls, so it is cited alongside TREK’s sensitive data handling.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is stored or transformed by RisingWave
IF retention or deletion expectations differ between the two systems
mitigations: Document which TREK data classes may enter RisingWave
Set a short retention window for any shared artifacts
Exclude secrets from analytics pipelines
Review logs for personal data exposure
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
